explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM predictions with human judgments on 100 sampled cases for both option conversion and expert rating tasks, reporting Pearson's r, Spearman's ρ, Kendall's τ correlations and accuracy metrics

prompts.notes: Paper states 'Details of our prompts for OC and ER are available in §G in the appendix.' Examples of option conversion are shown in Figure with response classification like 'Result: I score it as 3.9 (High)'

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: quadratic-weighted kappa used for ordinal classes

guidelines.notes: Paper provides human annotation example prompts with scoring scales, exemplar items, and scoring instructions; annotators were screened for character understanding

sample_size.notes: For each task (OC and ER), 100 cases of state-of-the-art RPAs on the BFI were manually labeled by humans for comparison with LLM predictions

quantitative_scores.notes: 82% of GPT-4 predictions rated as 'right' (deviation <1 point)
Only 4% of GPT-4 predictions were 'wrong' (deviation >1 point)

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 achieves the best performance with 82% accuracy and only 4% wrong cases in expert rating, primarily failing when RPAs give contradictory responses; state-of-the-art LLMs show adequate performance in simulating human interviewers

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLMs and humans evaluate personality fidelity using the same criteria and psychological scales
